messages:
maria: Customer ticket CS-4122 — multiple customers reporting sudden 401s from regenerated SDKs (python/ts) after yesterday's client-gen. They see retry storms and elevated billing. Raising for triage.

alex: Thanks — can you paste the exact error and a minimal repro? SDK versions involved?

sam: Repro'd locally. Minimal steps: pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0 then simple generate call fails. 1.3.4 works. Logs: 401 then client retries.

sam: Curl repro (redacted token):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"vicuna","input":"hello"}'
```

sam: Response headers/body: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"invalid auth header: missing x-api-key"}
```

alex: Interesting — server is expecting x-api-key. Did the OpenAPI auth scheme change in the regen? Which generator commit was used?

julia: I traced the client-gen run — generator image tag: ci/gen-2026-03-08. Looking at the spec diff we pushed last night, the securityScheme name was changed from "api_key" to "x-api-key" (see commit f7e9a2c -> 9b4f6d1). That would change the header param name in the generated clients.

support-bot: Noted: billing alert — unusual token usage spike attributed to repeated retries from some SDK versions (CS-4122).

sam: The problem appears in both python and ts clients where the runtime maps the configured token to the old header (Authorization) but server-side auth middleware now checks x-api-key header key. If both aren't accepted, requests 401 and SDK's built-in retry policy floods while client code retries automatically.

alex: Short-term mitigation: can we make the server accept Authorization as equivalent to x-api-key for a migration window? Also add retry cap on SDK to avoid billing spikes.

julia: I can add a server side header-alias patch — quick rule: if Authorization present and request lacks x-api-key, copy Authorization -> x-api-key before auth check. Patch would be trivial but we should avoid forever coupling.

ci-bot: Pipeline run triggered: regen-ci for client-gen. Commits to bisect: f7e9a2c..9b4f6d1.

sam: For longer term we need generator change: maintain previous security scheme name or add aliases in templates. Also add a unit test in regen CI that runs a tiny integration: generated client must authenticate against a mock auth server accepting old header.

alex: I'll open a devex PR to revert the scheme name in the OpenAPI spec and add the compatibility test in the regen pipeline. Also will add a temporary SDK backcompat layer that sends both headers for one minor release.

julia: Bisect notes: commit 9a3c5b7 in generator template swapped headerParam from "Authorization" to "x-api-key" due to a mis-merge with a downstream spec. Rolling back that template line fixes generated header mapping.

support-bot: CS ticket updated: mitigation steps posted to customer (recommend pinning to redwood-sdk==1.3.4 or temporarily allowing both headers).

alex: Action items: 1) server header-alias patch (julia) 2) revert spec name + regen test (alex) 3) SDK small patch to set both headers for v1.4.x (sam) 4) add CI test to prevent auth scheme renames (devex).

maria: I'll coordinate customer communication and confirm whether pinning client works for them. Keep me updated so I can close CS-4122.

ci-bot: regen-ci started: auth-header-backcompat test failing on current head (1 failure).

sam: Quick note — when patching SDK, also tighten retry policy (max_retries=3 default) to limit billing fallout.

alex: Agreed. I'll include retry cap in the SDK patch.

maria: Thanks all — ping me when PRs land so I can schedule a customer patch note. :thumbsup:
